title: Ultimate Homemade Pizza Dough
description: The kind that costs about $1.70 per large base but tastes like it should come with its own Italian soundtrack.

ingredients.item: water (cold for bread machine, lukewarm for hand mixing)

method.instruction: Bread Machine Method: Add all ingredients to the bread machine in the order recommended by your machine's manual (usually liquids first, then dry ingredients, with yeast on top).
Select the 'dough' setting and start. If needed, scrape down the sides with a silicone spatula during mixing.
Once the cycle is complete, remove dough and let it proof in a lightly oiled bowl covered with a damp tea towel for 30-60 minutes until puffy.
Hand Method: In a large bowl, combine lukewarm water, yeast, and a pinch of sugar. Let stand 5 minutes until foamy.
Add flour, salt, olive oil, and bread improver (if using). Mix until a rough dough forms.
Knead on a lightly floured surface for 8-10 minutes until smooth and elastic. The dough should be soft and slightly tacky but not sticky.
Place in a lightly oiled bowl, cover with a damp tea towel, and rest in a warm spot for 1-1.5 hours until doubled in size.
Punch down the dough and divide according to your needs: 1 family-sized pizza (full batch), 2 large pizzas (divide in half), or 4 personal pizzas (divide into quarters).
Shape each portion into a ball, cover, and let rest for 10-15 minutes to relax the gluten before rolling.
Roll out on a floured surface or stretch by hand to desired thickness. Top and bake at your preferred temperature (usually 220-250°C / 425-480°F).

notes.title: Flour Matters
notes.content: Baker's flour with 12-14% protein gives you the best structure and chew. Regular plain flour will work but won't have the same texture.

notes.title: Skip the Yeast?
notes.content: For a thin, crispy crust, you can skip the yeast entirely. The dough will be denser but still delicious — perfect for cracker-thin pizzas.

notes.title: Make Ahead
notes.content: Dough can be refrigerated for up to 3 days or frozen for up to 3 months. Thaw frozen dough overnight in the fridge before using.

notes.title: Final Word
notes.content: This isn't just dough — it's edible pride. Because frozen crusts have no soul. But clearly, you do.
